summary_html: A child dies or suffers serious harm while **under agency supervision**, constituting systemic failure. Federal law mandates disclosure and review to identify causes and reforms.
authority_html:
- **Protect Our Kids Act (PL 112-275)** — federal commission and review requirements  
- **CAPTA §5106a(b)(2)(A)(x)** — mandates public disclosure of child-fatality cases

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: Pittman v. Cuyahoga County Department of Children & Family Services
key_cases.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit
key_cases.holding: The Sixth Circuit reversed the denial of immunity, holding a social worker absolutely immune for the custody complaint, supporting affidavits and recommendations she filed with the juvenile court, even against allegations that she made intentional misrepresentations.
key_cases.relevance: Limits the damages remedy against caseworkers whose court submissions preceded a bad outcome.
key_cases.quote: Whether Hurry made intentional misrepresentations to the juvenile court in the complaint and affidavits does not affect the conclusion that she is entitled to absolute immunity.

key_cases.case_name: DeShaney v. Winnebago County Department of Social Services
key_cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States
key_cases.holding: The Supreme Court held that the Due Process Clause imposes no affirmative duty on a State to protect a child from private violence, so county social workers were not liable for failing to remove a child they knew was being abused.
key_cases.relevance: Sets the constitutional limit on section 1983 claims arising from a child's death under agency supervision.
key_cases.quote: nothing in the language of the Due Process Clause itself requires the State to protect the life, liberty, and property of its citizens against invasion by private actors

key_cases.holding: In a wrongful-death action arising from a fatal child abuse case, the court held that the reporting statute's immunity under Tenn. Code Ann. sec. 37-1-410(a) protects only persons who actually make a report of harm, and that the physician who did not report was not immune.
key_cases.relevance: Supplies Tennessee's rule on immunity in litigation following a child's death after an unreported disclosure.
key_cases.quote: immunity under Tennessee Code Annotated section 37-1-410(a) is afforded only to those who actually report harm

key_cases.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit
key_cases.holding: Sitting en banc, the Sixth Circuit reversed the grant of absolute immunity to a caseworker sued for concealing from the juvenile court that the mother wished to assert her parental rights, holding that absolute immunity reaches only functions performed as a legal advocate, while affirming judgment for the county.
key_cases.relevance: Supplies the test a family must satisfy to reach a caseworker in damages for conduct outside her advocacy role.
key_cases.quote: absolute immunity extends to social workers only when they are acting in the capacity of legal advocates
